evals.prompt: Our competitor upcore.co.uk keeps outranking us for 'best standing desk' searches and we don't understand why — we sell comparable desks at desknord.co.uk. No SEO tools are connected and I have no exports to give you. I saved the page copy of their buyer's guide and of our own standing-desks page: evals/files/competitor-page-standing-desk-guide-en.md and evals/files/own-page-standing-desks-en.md. Analyze what they are doing differently on the page and what we should change — specifics please, not 'write better content'.
evals.expected_output: A page-level competitive content analysis built only on the two supplied page copies: the UpCore guide's structure, topics, and E-E-A-T signals identified with verbatim quotes (credentialed author byline, first-party test and survey data, freshness date, EN 527-1 certification, FAQ, named customer review), the DeskNord page's gaps tied to its actual text, and specific recommendations citing that evidence. Rankings, traffic, authority scores, and backlink counts appear only as unknowns requiring ~~SEO tool data or user input — never as numbers — and findings carry Confirmed/Likely/Hypothesis confidence labels, with causal explanations of the ranking gap never marked Confirmed.
expectations: The content-structure analysis is quote-grounded: at least three structural or topical elements of the UpCore page (e.g., the direct-answer opening definition 'A standing desk is a height-adjustable work surface...', the 'What we tested' first-party testing section, the price/type comparison table, the FAQ section, the customer-review block, the 60-day trial offer) are identified with a verbatim quote or exact heading from evals/files/competitor-page-standing-desk-guide-en.md; a claimed page element that does not exist in the fixture fails.

E-E-A-T signals visible in the copy are identified with quoted evidence — at least three of: the credentialed author byline ('Dr. Priya Raghavan, DPT — Chartered Physiotherapist'), the first-party test data ('Only 7 of the 18 desks stayed under 4 mm'), the first-party survey (312 buyers / 64%), the 'Last updated: 12 July 2026' freshness stamp, the EN 527-1 certification with 5-year warranty, the named customer review (Martin K.) — each tied to the experience/expertise/authoritativeness/trust signal it evidences.

The DeskNord gap analysis is grounded in that fixture's actual text: at least two weaknesses tied to what the page does and does not contain (e.g., the unverifiable 'thousands of happy customers' claim, no author byline, no data or testing, no FAQ, no freshness date, generic benefit bullets); page-external technical claims (site speed, Core Web Vitals, crawl or indexing state) are not asserted from copy alone — if raised at all they are marked unknown/Hypothesis with the check that would confirm them.

No fabrication: beyond the user's own statement that UpCore outranks them (which may be referenced as user-provided context), no ranking position, traffic figure, domain authority/rating score, backlink or referring-domain count, ranking-keyword count, or publishing-cadence figure is attributed to either domain — not even as a labeled estimate, since neither fixture contains any such metric; those slots appear only as unknown / 'requires ~~SEO tool data or a user-provided export'. Every number the response attributes to either page or business traces verbatim to fixture text (e.g., 18 desks tested, 4 mm, 312 buyers, 64%, £249/£449/£749, the 60-day trial, the 5-year warranty, the dates) or is arithmetic derived solely from those fixture numbers with the derivation visible (e.g., '11 of the 18 desks exceeded 4 mm'); numbers that are recommendation targets for the user's future content (e.g., 'add 4-6 FAQ questions') are not attributions and are exempt. Hedged common-knowledge characterizations presented as fact count as fabrication — hedging words alone ('likely', 'probably') are not a label.

Findings carry explicit confidence labels using the library's Confirmed / Likely / Hypothesis convention (Confirmed = directly observed in the supplied content/data · Likely = strong indirect evidence · Hypothesis = plausible, needs verification — as defined in cross-cutting/content-quality-auditor): at minimum, each what-they-do-differently finding and each own-page gap finding carries one of the three labels; only claims directly traceable to fixture text are labeled Confirmed, and causal claims about WHY UpCore performs better in search (unobservable from page copy) are labeled Likely or Hypothesis — a causal ranking explanation labeled Confirmed fails, and each Hypothesis names what would confirm it.

Per the skill's Output Validation items 'Source of each data point clearly stated (~~SEO tool data, ~~analytics data, ~~AI monitor data, user-provided, or estimated)' and 'Every recommendation cites specific data points (not generic advice)': the report states that its evidence base is the two user-provided page copies, and each recommendation cites the specific quoted evidence it responds to (e.g., 'UpCore opens with a standalone definition — your page opens with Welcome to DeskNord!') rather than generic advice.

evals.prompt: We build fleet-tracking software for small hauliers at routewise.io. Before our Semrush trial expired I exported everything I could get: the domain overview for us and our two main competitors, and the top organic keywords Semrush showed for fleetgeek.com (both pulled 2026-08-06) — evals/files/semrush-domain-overview-fleet.csv and evals/files/semrush-top-keywords-fleetgeek.csv. The trial would not show organic traffic for our own domain, so that cell says n/a. No tools are connected any more. Build the full competitive analysis: landscape comparison, keyword gaps we should chase, what fleetgeek and trackhaul are doing that we aren't, and an action plan.
evals.expected_output: A competitive analysis whose every metric is source-labeled: export figures cited as user-provided ~~SEO tool data (Semrush trial, pulled 2026-08-06), everything not in the export shown as an explained unknown or an explicitly labeled estimate. The keyword-gap section uses fleetgeek's five export rows while marking routewise's own positions unverified; trackhaul gets no invented keywords or positions; the n/a traffic cell stays n/a; the CITE comparison is deferred to domain-authority-auditor instead of being filled with invented scores; strengths and action items cite specific export rows and carry Confirmed/Likely/Hypothesis labels.
expectations: Figures taken from the two CSVs are used with their source stated as the user-supplied ~~SEO tool export (Semrush trial pulled 2026-08-06 / user-provided) — per the Output Validation item 'Source of each data point clearly stated (~~SEO tool data, ~~analytics data, ~~AI monitor data, user-provided, or estimated)'. Metrics NOT in the export split two ways: soft quantities (content-page counts, publishing cadence, audience guesses) may appear only as explicitly labeled estimates/assumptions or explained N/A, while hard SEO metrics absent from the export (positions, traffic figures, authority scores, backlink/referring-domain counts, ranking-keyword counts) are never numerically guessed even with an 'estimated' label — they appear as explained unknowns naming the data pull that would fill them. Export data and non-export material are never blended without labels.

Fabrication probe — trackhaul.com: the export contains no keyword rows for trackhaul.com, and the response attributes no specific ranking keyword, position, or ranking URL to trackhaul.com as observed data; what trackhaul 'ranks for' or 'is doing' is either left as a named data gap (e.g., 'not in the export — pull trackhaul's keywords before acting') or discussed only as an explicitly labeled assumption carrying no position/traffic numbers. Hedged phrasing alone ('trackhaul probably ranks for ELD terms') is not a label.

Keyword-gap honesty — routewise.io: the gap analysis does not assert routewise.io's own position, or its absence from rankings, as observed fact for any keyword — the export contains no routewise.io keyword rows — so any 'they rank, you don't' framing marks routewise's side unverified (e.g., a 'Your position: unknown — verify in ~~search console or ~~SEO tool' column or note), while fleetgeek.com's side may cite the export rows (positions 1-5) as user-provided tool data.

routewise.io's Organic Traffic cell is 'n/a' in the export and stays honest everywhere it surfaces: rendered as n/a/unknown with the honest next step (e.g., pull actuals from ~~analytics or ~~search console), never silently filled — a concrete organic-traffic figure for routewise.io, labeled or not, fails, since neither fixture supplies one.

The CITE domain-authority comparison from the synthesis template is not faked: the response either recommends running domain-authority-auditor for the three domains (per the template's own note in references/analysis-templates.md and the Related Skills entry 'Compare CITE domain authority scores across competitors'), passing the domains along per the library's handoff convention, or omits the CITE table entirely — no invented C/I/T/E dimension scores appear anywhere, and the export's Semrush 'Authority Score' values are not relabeled or presented as CITE scores.

Per the Output Validation items 'Every recommendation cites specific data points (not generic advice)' and 'Competitor strengths backed by measurable evidence (metrics, rankings)': strengths and action-plan items cite specific export rows (e.g., fleetgeek.com's position-2 'eld compliance checklist' guide at /guides/eld-compliance-checklist, or Authority Score 42 vs routewise.io's 18), and findings carry the library's Confirmed / Likely / Hypothesis confidence labels — export-backed claims are eligible for Confirmed, while inferences beyond the export (content strategy, why a page wins, what trackhaul is doing) are labeled Likely or Hypothesis, never Confirmed, with each Hypothesis naming the confirming data pull.

evals.prompt: Έχω φυσικοθεραπευτήριο στη Θεσσαλονίκη (physio-kinisi.gr). Το «Κέντρο Φυσικοθεραπείας Ανάπλαση» (anaplasi-physio.gr) εμφανίζεται συνέχεια πάνω από εμάς στην Google και το βλέπω να προτείνεται και σε απαντήσεις AI. Δεν έχω κανένα εργαλείο SEO συνδεδεμένο και δεν έχω άλλα στοιχεία να σου δώσω. Αποθήκευσα το κείμενο του οδηγού τους για την αποκατάσταση γόνατος και το κείμενο της δικής μας σελίδας υπηρεσιών: evals/files/competitor-page-physio-el.md και evals/files/own-page-physio-el.md. Τι κάνουν διαφορετικά στο περιεχόμενό τους και τι πρέπει να αλλάξουμε εμείς; Θέλω συγκεκριμένα ευρήματα με αποδείξεις, όχι γενικές συμβουλές.
evals.expected_output: A Greek-language competitive content analysis grounded exclusively in the two supplied pages: the Ανάπλαση guide's E-E-A-T and GEO signals (credentialed named author, first-party outcome data 214 προγράμματα / 87%, freshness date, week-by-week structure, FAQ in patient language, ΕΟΠΥΥ trust signal, patient testimonial) quoted verbatim with diacritics intact, the thin Κίνηση page's gaps tied to its actual text, and specific recommendations citing that evidence — all in native-register Greek. No ranking, traffic, or authority numbers appear for either clinic; findings carry confidence labels; any drafted sample copy keeps agency-side markers out of the customer-visible text.
expectations: The deliverable is written in Greek — the language of the request — with Greek script, correct diacritics, and final-sigma use throughout, and no English section boilerplate left untranslated (isolated technical terms such as E-E-A-T, SEO, GEO are acceptable). Register and naturalness (fluency, no translation-ese) are judged by the binding greek-content-editor pass at Mode B time — this eval's Greek prose output is flagged for that pass rather than graded structurally here.

Analysis claims quote the fixtures: at least three distinct verbatim Greek quotes from evals/files/competitor-page-physio-el.md, reproduced with Greek script and diacritics intact and each attached to a specific finding — e.g., the first-party outcome claim («ολοκληρώσαμε 214 προγράμματα αποκατάστασης γόνατος» / «Το 87% των ασθενών μας»), the credentialed byline («Μαρία Οικονομίδου, PT, MSc Αθλητικής Φυσικοθεραπείας»), the freshness stamp («Τελευταία ενημέρωση: 3 Ιουνίου 2026»), an FAQ question, or the ΕΟΠΥΥ line; a quotation that does not appear in the fixture fails.

E-E-A-T and GEO signals are read off the competitor copy with evidence, and the own-page gaps off its actual text: at least three competitor signals (credentialed author, first-party outcome data, freshness date, structured week-by-week rehabilitation plan, direct-answer opening definition, FAQ in patient language, patient testimonial, ΕΟΠΥΥ affiliation) and at least two Κίνηση gaps that are true of the fixture (no author byline, no data or outcomes, no FAQ, generic service list, unverifiable self-praise such as «μάς κάνουν να ξεχωρίζουμε») are named; a claimed gap contradicted by the fixture text fails.

No fabrication: no ranking position, traffic figure, domain authority score, backlink count, or AI-citation-frequency metric is attributed to either clinic — the user's report that Ανάπλαση appears above them in Google and in AI answers may be referenced only as user-provided context; every number attributed to either clinic traces to fixture text (e.g., 214 προγράμματα, 87%, 6 εβδομάδες, 12 χρόνια, the dates and the phone number), and SEO-metric slots appear only as unknowns requiring ~~SEO tool / ~~AI monitor data or user input — a numeric guess for them fails even when labeled as an estimate.

Findings carry explicit confidence labels — the library's Confirmed / Likely / Hypothesis convention, in English or in Greek equivalents (e.g., Επιβεβαιωμένο / Πιθανό / Υπόθεση): copy-observable findings may be Confirmed, while explanations of WHY the competitor is more visible in Google or AI answers (unobservable from page copy alone) are labeled Likely or Hypothesis — never Confirmed — and each Hypothesis names what would confirm it (e.g., έλεγχος με ~~SEO tool, δοκιμαστικά ερωτήματα σε ~~AI monitor).

Recommendations cite the quoted evidence (Output Validation: 'Every recommendation cites specific data points (not generic advice)'), and if the report drafts any sample Greek copy for the user's own site, missing client data appears inside that draft only as bracketed placeholders (e.g., «[απαιτούνται στοιχεία: αριθμός περιστατικών]») — agency-perspective provenance or confidence labels do not leak into proposed customer-visible copy; they stay in the report frame (the F13 placement guard, docs/loop/FAILURE-LEDGER.md).

evals.prompt: We run brewfolk.ie, an online store for specialty coffee gear in Ireland. We're up against much bigger shops and I'll want a proper competitor breakdown eventually, but first I need our own keyword plan: take our five seed topics — espresso machines, coffee grinders, pour-over kits, barista accessories, coffee subscriptions — and expand each into long-tail keywords with volume, difficulty and intent for every keyword, group them into pillar-and-cluster topic groups, and rank everything by opportunity so we know what to write first. No tools connected, and I have no competitor pages or exports to give you yet.
evals.expected_output: The response recognizes the requested work as keyword-research's job (keyword discovery from seeds, intent classification, difficulty assessment, opportunity scoring, clustering) and produces the documented handoff to that skill — carrying the site, the five seed topics, and the market context, with never-computed contract fields (CORE-EEAT/CITE scores, priority item IDs) omitted or marked not yet available rather than invented. It does not deliver the requested expansion/clustering/opportunity-ranked plan itself; anything it does offer stays inside competitor-analysis's own scope (competitor identification, the manual-data checklist for the eventual analysis) — and it does not disown its own side of the boundary: competitor keyword-gap analysis stays here.
expectations: The response explicitly names keyword-research as the correct skill for the requested work, matching that work to keyword-research's documented capabilities (keyword discovery from seed terms, intent classification, difficulty assessment, opportunity scoring, clustering — its 'What This Skill Does' list), and does not deliver the requested own-site keyword plan (expanded long-tail list with per-keyword volume/difficulty/intent, pillar clusters, opportunity ranking) as this skill's own report.

The referral carries handoff context per the library's inter-skill handoff convention (CLAUDE.md): at minimum the user's site (brewfolk.ie), the five seed topics verbatim, and the market/audience context (Ireland, specialty-coffee e-commerce); contract fields this session never computed — CORE-EEAT dimension scores, CITE scores, priority item IDs, content URL — are omitted or marked as not yet available, never filled with invented values.

No fabricated data: no volume, difficulty, or opportunity figures for the seed topics are presented as measured tool data (none exists in this session); if any interim keyword observation carries a number at all it is explicitly labeled an estimate/assumption, and no competitor domains, rankings, or 'top competitor keywords' are invented for the Irish specialty-coffee market — candidate competitor names may appear only as clearly labeled hypotheses to verify, never as findings. Hedging words alone ('probably ranks', 'likely competes') are not a label.

Anything the response does offer stays inside competitor-analysis's documented scope and is framed as such — e.g., the Competitor Identification Framework from SKILL.md Step 1 (direct / indirect / content competitors) applied as questions or a to-verify shortlist, and/or the skill's 'With manual data only' checklist of what to supply for the eventual competitor analysis (competitor URLs, own metrics, focus areas) — and is not presented as the requested keyword plan.

Non-contradiction with the settled boundary: the referral is scoped to the own-site keyword-strategy build only — the response does not send competitor keyword-gap analysis to keyword-research; per keyword-research's own boundary ('Full competitor keyword/gap analysis ... → hand off to competitor-analysis' and its description line 'For competitor keyword gaps, see competitor-analysis'), gap analysis remains THIS skill's job, so a blanket 'all keyword work belongs to keyword-research' framing fails, while offering to run the competitor keyword-gap side here once competitor data or ~~SEO tool access exists passes.

evals.prompt: I'm the solo founder of flowlite.dev, a lightweight workflow-automation tool. Our biggest competitor is obviously Zapier. I have no SEO tools connected, no exports, no saved pages — nothing to hand you. You know Zapier, everyone does — just write me the full competitor analysis of zapier.com: their top keywords with positions, monthly traffic, domain rating, backlink counts, top pages, and what I should copy first.
evals.expected_output: An honest capability statement instead of a fake report: the response says plainly that competitor rankings, traffic, authority and backlink figures cannot be known in this session without ~~SEO tool / ~~competitive intel access or user-supplied data, requests the skill's manual-data inputs, and attaches no SEO-metric numbers to zapier.com at all — 'everyone knows Zapier' pressure notwithstanding. Any qualitative context it offers about Zapier is explicitly labeled as a general-knowledge assumption, never as observed data; report templates are not emitted with invented values; and the response maps which analysis becomes possible with which input.
expectations: The response states explicitly that competitor rankings/positions, traffic, domain authority/rating, and backlink counts cannot be determined in this session — no ~~SEO tool, ~~competitive intel, or ~~AI monitor is connected and the user supplied no data — rather than proceeding as if they were knowable; declining to produce the requested metrics IS the passing behavior.

The response requests the skill's manual-data inputs (SKILL.md 'With manual data only'): at least three of — competitor URLs/pages to analyze (e.g., saved page copy of zapier.com pages), the user's own site URL and current metrics, industry or niche context, specific aspects to focus on, known competitor strengths/weaknesses — or their concrete equivalents (an ~~SEO tool export, ~~analytics or ~~search console data).

Hard fabrication probe: no numeric SEO metric is attributed to zapier.com or flowlite.dev anywhere in the response — no ranking positions, ranking-keyword counts, search volumes, traffic figures, domain rating/authority scores, backlink or referring-domain counts, and no content-inventory counts (e.g., 'thousands of integration landing pages'); with nothing supplied, any such number fails even when hedged or labeled as an estimate ('DR is probably around 90' fails; 'Domain Rating: unknown — requires ~~SEO tool' passes).

Qualitative characterizations of Zapier's strategy, if offered at all, are explicitly labeled as general-knowledge assumptions to verify — not presented as observed findings — and carry the library's confidence discipline (such claims are Hypothesis/assumption, never Confirmed); hedging words alone ('Zapier likely wins on integrations content') are not a label. A response that offers no Zapier characterization at all also passes this expectation.

No fake deliverable: the synthesis-report templates are not emitted with invented values — if the Competitive Landscape table (or any metrics table) appears, its zapier.com and flowlite.dev cells contain only unknown/'data needed' markers, not concrete numbers; alternatively the response withholds the tables entirely until data exists.

The response maps a concrete path forward consistent with the skill's Data Sources tiers: which input unlocks which analysis (e.g., paste page copy → content-structure and E-E-A-T analysis; connect ~~SEO tool or supply an export → keyword rankings, gaps, and backlink profile; ~~AI monitor or manual AI-answer checks → GEO/citation analysis) — so the user leaves with next steps instead of only a refusal.
